title: Accordion of collapsible sections
when: The user wants stacked sections that expand and collapse, for long content, settings groups or step details.
inputs: whether only one may be open at a time
prompt:
Goal: Sections that expand in place with the right semantics, optional motion and deep links.
Steps:
1. Simple case: native <details><summary>; give grouped details the same name attribute when only one may be open.
2. Custom case: an h3 wrapping <button type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="sec-1">, then <div id="sec-1" role="region" aria-labelledby hidden>.
3. Rotate an aria-hidden chevron on [aria-expanded="true"] or details[open].
4. Animate with a grid wrapper from grid-template-rows: 0fr to 1fr; drop the transition under prefers-reduced-motion.
5. If location.hash matches a section id on load, open it and scroll to it.
Quality bar:
- The whole header row is the click target.
- Content in a closed section is out of the Tab order.
- Headings keep the page outline in order.
Pitfalls:
- Clickable divs with no keyboard support.
- Animating max-height to a huge value.
- Removing the summary marker with no visible cue left.
Verify:
- [ ] Every toggle is a button or a summary.
- [ ] aria-expanded matches the visible state.
- [ ] aria-controls ids exist and are unique.
- [ ] Reduced motion stops the animation.
Output: Accordion markup in the page, its CSS, and accordion.js only for the custom variant.

examples.input: accordion for course modules, only one open at a time
examples.output: details elements sharing name="modules", summary with module title and duration, rotating chevron
